utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning to you, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you follow the proceedings in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I can. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, Anna Richterova, Julian Nicholls and Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. And good morning to you all. Appearances for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Attorney at law Milan Trbojevic, appearing with me today is Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good morning to you both. So I understand there is some problem? Shall we go in private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: If we can go to private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'll ask you to repeat your solemn declaration once more, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And once again only the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Let's proceed. It's your turn now, Mr. Trbojevic. Please remember not to mention the witness's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we've gone into open.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, your microphone is not on, Mr. Trbojevic. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Trbojevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you to start with that part of your yesterday's testimony with which we haven't finished, when I made an objection to a part of the record. You testified about an event of 23rd of June, 1992. That's page 5 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could show the witness his statement, Your Honours. That's the statement from the 8th of April, 1992 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have a copy of the 8 April, 2000 statement. I'll just tell the Court and counsel, this doesn't have any writing on it, it does have a -- there is a plain copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is your own statement. Would you be so kind as to look at page 5, paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You started describing events that preceded the incidents of that night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you had seen people gathered near the house of Meho Alic. You said there were about 120 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, concerning (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were observing there from a distance of about 400 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, (Redacted) (Redacted)?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So that will be redacted as well as what I have just stated myself before Mr. Nicholls confirmed, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You continued to describe what happened later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that that evening, sometime about 11.30 p.m., you heard the sound of tractors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, that's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you concluded that it was on those tractors that women and children were taken away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was able to conclude that at that time, and I heard from other people later that it was true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then we come to the description of the events of that night. In this statement, from April 2000, you speak about a -- about the time of 3:00, 4:00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page is that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 8, paragraph 5. You said you heard bursts of gunfire around 3.00 a.m., maybe 4.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday, you said these bursts of gunfire were heard about 1.00, 1.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't understand me, then. Around 12.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's not an objection, Your Honour but my colleague and the witness are speaking over each other not allowing each other to finish so I think the interpreters are doing well but I'm afraid that something may get lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was finding difficulty myself and I realise the interpreters are finding difficulty. Mr. Trbojevic, you are familiar with what I am saying but the witness is not. You speak the same language, both Mr. Trbojevic and yourself, and what's happening is that Mr. Trbojevic is not allowing an interval of time after you finish answering one of his questions. He jumps in with the next question and you are doing exactly the same. You are not allowing a short interval of time when he finishes his question before you start your answer. Procedure here is that while you speak in your language, we have teams of interpreters translating into English and into French that need to catch up with you. So please slow down, both of you, and allow an interval between question and answer and between answer and question. Okay? Thanks. And thank you, Mr. Nicholls, because you preceded me by just a minute or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have to object to the record, on page 8, line 4, my question was not recorded correctly. It's not page 8. It's page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 6 or page 8? Page 6? How can it be page 6?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: In the question of council, page 8 is mentioned in the record whereas it should be page 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 6, page 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 8 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 6 or page 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: Page 6 of the transcript should be mentioned in my question, whereas on the record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... paragraph 5, you mean to say page 6, paragraph 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, page 6, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That goes for the record. But in any case, he did give you an answer. All right. Now, please repeat your next question now. You asked the witness, "In your testimony yesterday," referring to page 6, paragraph 5, "You said that bursts of gunfire were heard about, here we have 1.00, 1.30 a.m., and then the witness butted in saying you don't understand me then. It was around 12.30 a.m. So pick it up from there, please, and go ahead with your question and then the witness will answer. All right? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what I wanted to clarify. At 2330 hours you heard the sound of tractors. That was the time when women and children were probably leaving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We have a misunderstanding again. Around 11.30 p.m., that is the time when women and children were leaving.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At what time did you hear the burst of gunfire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two to three minutes, for about two to three minutes, around 1.00 a.m. That is the time when I left the place where I was until then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You described how during that shooting, you were lying down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you heard bullets whizzing around you. You said you didn't see who was doing what on the site?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the people who were shooting are not in your field of vision at that moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't tell us how many of them there were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't tell you that because I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us were they in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that either because I wasn't able to see them that morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can't describe for us their position relative to the people who were probably victims? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't do that either because from my position I wasn't able to see them, when I was lying down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether in that darkness and in that position, was it possible for anyone to run away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I kept asking myself: Why, out of those 27 people, why didn't a single person try to escape? Unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking about the 27 people, you didn't establish that number by counting them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't actually count them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I know how many people were gone missing and that's why I assumed that they are the same people, that there are 27 of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to hear any orders issued?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't. All I heard was singing, racket, but I didn't hear any orders being issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On page 6 of this statement of yours, paragraph 7, you explain that it was practically in the morning from a distance of 500 metres you saw a group of soldiers in that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, we are talking about 500 metres as the crow flies. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then on page 7, paragraph 1, you describe how in addition to those soldiers, you said I saw objects on the ground that looked like sacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sacks. From that distance of 500 metres it looked like sacks, whether it was victims, whether it was objects, lying on the ground, I don't know. All I know is I saw a couple of soldiers milling about them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure that yesterday during the examination by the Prosecutor you gave the same statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you understood it correctly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, the record does not reflect such a statement. The record says that you had seen bodies lying around like sacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they looked like sacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to ask you the following question: Are you aware of the fact that this statement is significantly different from the previous one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference. However, I abide by what I said. I said that it looked like sacks and I also said that it was my opinion that those were people. It would have been impossible for sacks to be lying around at that time. I cannot state with certainty what it was but it was my assumption that those were the victims, as it turned out later on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe we have clarified the issue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you are clear about it, I think we have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those objects that you saw, where were they, where did they lie?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that same area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, near the cemetery, where those two graves were, which I saw personally where the excavator was digging. I think I saw the photograph of the location yesterday. I can show the location once again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you indicated that during the exhumation, as you learned later on, five bodies were discovered, five bodies that were identified as possible victims of that incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Five victims, one skull and parts of bones. However, I wonder, and I should like to ask all of you present here in the courtroom, what happened, then, with other people, with the remaining people?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask you. Do you have any knowledge to the effect that the number of bodies that may have been moved to another grave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have any personal knowledge. I can only assume that the majority of people had been killed and buried there, but their bodies must have been transferred somewhere else. Again this is just my opinion. I do not have any accurate information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe the issue is now clear, as clear as possible, that is. Let me remind you of the portion of your statement when you indicated that movement permits were issued only to Muslims, that only Muslims had to have such permits. Do you remember that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, that was not entirely the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to the best of my knowledge, that indeed was the case. I have -- I had Serb friends, I have Serb friends today, but at the time they did not have to have such permits, sir. I'm sure you were there at the time, as well, and you did not have to have such a permit. I state this with full responsibility. That was not only my personal case. All Muslim residents had to have such permits, and I believe I have proved this claim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that all conscripts, mobilised to a military unit had to have permits for movement outside their military unit, permits which were issued by military authorities, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's possible, in case of military authorities, but I had a pass, a permit, which was issued by civilian authorities, by the police. However, it didn't mean anything. It was on my name and it was considered to be some kind of certificate, but it was actually useless.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I tell you that the people who were not members of the military, who were working, for instance, in the law enforcement organs or in the local administration, that they also had to have documents certifying that they were under some kind of work obligation and that on the basis of those documents they could not be mobilised into the army, and that they used such documents to move around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that they had similar documents but their documents did not have the same meaning. The names were indicative of who you were. There is a clear difference between my name and your name and I'm sure you understand this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you had obtained the documents that we had opportunity to see here and is it your opinion that those documents were just part of the special treatment that you received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, they were issued only for the purposes of identifying Muslims. One could not move around. One could not leave the area. You couldn't travel to Croatia from Bosanski Novi, for instance. Such documents were actually never checked so the objective was actually I don't know, I don't know whether it was money or something else. I don't know what the purpose of those documents was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I had the impression that yesterday you stated that the money should not have been the reason because the local currency was practically worthless?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was worthless but it was still better than nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it happen for the -- that the Croatian authorities asked for any such documents at the time you were entering the country?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because we left the area in an United Nations convoy. Nobody asked to see any documents. At least not in my case, and in that -- and in that part of the truck where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that there were no passports, no visas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no passports, no visas, we were on this convoy and no one asked any documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone check your identification cards when you came to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody asked to see any documents in the part of the truck where I was. Whether that was the case in some other truck, I don't know, but I don't think it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have your documents with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And I still have these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the residence certificates and the certificates of cancellation of residence, there is no need to look at them again, would you agree with me that such documents, such forms, are normally used in Bosnia-Herzegovina whenever one changes residence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is true. However, there is a special certificate, a special form, which was issued with these other documents, which had not been the case before. This particular certificate testified to the fact that we were relinquishing our property and it was with this document that we had to have these other residence documents. I know that there were the same documents existed before. However, this special certificate was not in use. The one that we had to have this time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you about a residence documents that was also part of that group of documents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 2, page 7 of your statement, you said that only Muslims were requested to surrender weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. What paragraph are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 2, paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the one starting with the Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one but the last paragraph, Bosanski Novi had a radio station in Novi town. I often listened to in April 1992. I heard radio broadcasts announcing that Muslims should surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I personally heard this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was only Muslims who were requested to surrender their weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only Muslims, 99 per cent. It was specially emphasised, Muslims and Muslim extremists. That is what I heard personally. However, on the same radio, and I don't think that this is in my statement, maybe it is, but the same radio broadcast, the news about a woman who had been killed in Ekici. However, they also stated that the perpetrator was unknown. However, everyone, including the police in Bosanski Novi, knew who it was. So for a radio station, for media, to declare that the perpetrator was unknown, I do not consider that to be a radio station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I must admit that I'm not aware of the incident you're talking about, and I do not wish to enter into any debate, nor do I have any right to do so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you provoked my reaction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just wanted to remind you that over that radio and in the media, generally speaking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... calm down, both of you. And neither of you has any right to react. This is a court of law, court of justice, where counsel for the Defence has every right to put questions to you on cross-examination, and you have a responsibility to answer those questions in a calm way, as -- and in a gentlemanly way, respectful way. I will stop Mr. Trbojevic if he is not respectful to you and I will stop you if you are not respectful to him. So please go ahead, Mr. Trbojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I did not interpret the witness's response as being an angry one or a misunderstanding. I don't think that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: From here, we can feel it heating up, Mr. Trbojevic. All right. So calm down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's just the way we talk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just wanted to remind you, Witness, that the same radio, well the one that we had at the time, and the newspapers, also appealed to the Serb population to surrender their weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I did not hear that with my own ears, that the Serbs were requested to surrender weapons. I think you know it yourself, that every Serb had the right to possess a rifle. Let me just give you one example. If I had a legally owned pistol and if you had one too, mine would have been seized and confiscated and what about -- why wasn't your pistol confiscated? This is just a simple example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we show Exhibit P1626 to the witness, please? The article. On the right side of the paper, you will see an article in which it is stated that Mr. Dejanovic and Mehmedagic had made a joint statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I personally did not hear this. Once again, I had Serb friends, I still have Serb friends, but none of them told me anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the article states that Dejanovic was appealing to the Serb population to surrender illegally owned weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they could have written anything, but what I'm telling you is that I personally never heard of any such case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a number of documents on evidence which demonstrate the fact that even the military requested certain units to be disarmed and -- so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour I object to the form of the question saying that there are a number of documents which demonstrate so and so. I think he should put the documents directly to the witness. He can summarise those documents and say, would you agree that this is true or so on, but I object to the representation that something has already been proven in evidence that this witness has never seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Objection sustained. You can't formulate your question the way you did, Mr. Trbojevic. You have to formulate it in the manner that has been suggested to you by Mr. Nicholls. If you have documents -- if you have documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was trying to save time, Your Honour. P227, please, if it can be shown to the witness? We no longer need that one. The Official Gazette; is that right? Under number 7, please, the conclusions. I know that this is not a particularly legible copy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure but it is the section under number 7. If -- perhaps I can have a look at it. I think I'll be able to locate it. If it's not a problem, can we please hear first two or three sentences? Does it say that "The Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region is hereby extending the deadline for the surrender of weapons, and that the request concerns all ethnicities"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but that was not the case in practice. I mean, you have to admit it yourself. You know that that was not the case in reality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Trbojevic is not giving evidence, sir. It's you who is giving evidence, not Mr. Trbojevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that's why I want to point out the fact that that was not the case in practice. This applied only to the Muslim people. Why am I saying this? I'm saying this because in 1992, and I'm sure you know this, everyone had a rifle and a green uniform. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the point has been made, Mr. Trbojevic. I think the point has been made that there is a conflict between you and the witness on this issue, and I think it's not going to change. So let's move to something else. You are right in that there are documents which do not distinguish between Muslims and other ethnicities but the witness is telling you that in practice, however, it was not like that. So I suggest you take up some other issue and you put a different question on another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We no longer need the document, but if I may ask just one additional question concerning this particular issue?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can we agree that as far as the unequal treatment is concerned, one of the reasons was the fact that the majority of Serbs had been mobilised and had some kind of military assignment, and on the basis of that, they had to keep their weapons, unlike Muslims who had not been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure you know this better than I do, but why only Muslims? Why wasn't I given a military assignment or a military obligation? Why? Not only myself but many others did not have such an assignment. That too was a problem and I asked you a moment ago if you had a pistol and if I had a pistol, too, why was mine confiscated and yours wasn't? If you're claiming that the treatment was equal, but it wasn't. You have to admit that it wasn't. I'm not trying to say that all Serbs were the same. Once again, I still have friends amongst them. But certain individuals committed certain things and they should be held accountable, and it will all become clear one day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will no longer deal with the weapons. You mentioned (Redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: (Redacted)in one of your statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this part has to be redacted because otherwise, his identity will be revealed so --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Maybe we should go into private. I don't know -- I don't presume to know what the line of question will be but...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We haven't been asked to go to private session. You know that whenever we are asked by Prosecution and by Defence we do go into private session. But in the meantime this has been stated by Mr. Trbojevic in open session and it needs to be redacted. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] (Redacted) (Redacted) maybe we can move into private session for a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But this also needs to be redacted. So this last sentence, which Mr. Trbojevic pronounced --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Needs to be redacted and we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. In the course of the events that you have testified upon, do you fit in any one by the name of Gvozden?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a Gvozden. There are even two of them, two brothers, one named Ranko and the other's name I don't know. They too were involved in this part, in these events. However, there is a Bogdan, I believe his surname is Grab, I'm not sure because I'm not a local --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You mentioned Bogdan Grab yesterday but I'm asking you about Gvozden.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is a Gvozden. In fact two brothers Gvozden, who were involved, but I didn't see them with my own eyes. I didn't see anything personally that would help me testify to that involvement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm asking you because in one of your statements to the Prosecution, Prosecutor, namely that of the 26th June of last year, of 2002, while you refer to your previous statement, namely that of April the 8th of the year 2000, you state the name Rajko Karlica should be changed into Ranko Gvozden everywhere in the statement. Did you actually make this correction or is this correction the result of a misunderstanding or a mistake made by who was interviewing you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not change my mind. I asked for this correction because I was not sure about the surname, whether it was Gvozden or Karlica. However, I know exactly which man I mean. There is also a Ranko Gvozden. I'm not sure only whether this one's surname too is Gvozden. I learned later that his last name is Karlica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That clears up the terrain for us. And I refer you to a question that was put to you earlier on today by Mr. Trbojevic, and your answer in respect of that question. You were asked to refer to the exhumation, and you said, "Yes, five victims, one skull and parts of bones. However, I wonder, and I should like to ask all of you present here in the courtroom, what happened then with the other people, with the remaining people"? And Mr. Trbojevic told you that's what I wanted to ask you. Do you have any knowledge to the effect that a number of bodies may have been moved to another grave? And you answered, "I do not have any personal knowledge. I can only assume that the majority of people had been killed and buried there. But their bodies must have been transferred somewhere else." Again, this is just my opinion,. I do not have any accurate information". In your statement to the Prosecutor in April of the year 2000, referring to the exhumation of the mass grave that we were talking about, you say, "I have learned that only five human remains were exhumed and have since been identified. During the exhumation, one human head and one arm was also exhumed. I have also heard that before the exhumation was carried out, Serbs had robbed the grave -- the mass grave and succeeded in removing most of the bodies." Did you make this last statement to the interviewing officer or not? And if you did, how do you reconcile it or how would you explain the testimony that you gave earlier on today? Because forming an opinion is one thing, being told by others that the Serbs had removed some of the remains is another thing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said this was my assumption, because I saw with my own eyes the excavator working on the site. There were two graves. It's impossible for only five bodies to be buried there, even a child can understand this. However, later, when these investigators came to exhume the bodies, there must have been an order issued to this effect. The bodies must have been removed and taken somewhere else. It's clear that such large graves, two of them, would not have been dug for only five bodies. That's what I'm trying to say. If all these people were killed, why didn't they leave them lying where they were? Why don't we know to this day where they are?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But in your statement you said, "I have also heard that before the exhumation was carried out, Serbs had robbed the mass grave and succeeded in removing --" Where did you hear this from? Did you actually hear from someone that the Serbs had desecrated this mass grave and removed most of the bodies or you just made that up in your mind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BT84 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in my mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. That explains it. Okay. I don't see that there are further questions and that means that your testimony comes to an end here. You are free now to return to your country of residence and for this purpose you will be assisted, given all Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the assistance, help you require by this Tribunal. Before you are ushered out of this courtroom, it is my duty as the Presiding Judge, in my name and on behalf of the two Judges, Judge Janu and Judge Taya who are hearing this case with me, to thank you, also on behalf of the Tribunal in general, for having accepted to come over and give evidence. Last thing is I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you sincerely for this. I apologise if I spoke out of turn or too fast or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't always feel too comfortable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we now have BT49?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and she was granted closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Closed session. This witness has already been granted closed session as a protective measure and I'm pretty sure that members of the public in the public gallery will understand the reason for this is to protect the witness, with the result, however, that they will not be able to follow the proceedings. Let's go into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
